definitions.explanation: A writing system of raised dots read by touch, used by blind and partially sighted people.

examples.japanese: {点字|てんじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}める→読む：00426_yomu⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なりたい→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: I want to learn to read Braille.

examples.japanese: ⟦エレベーター→エレベーター：01340_erebeetaa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ボタン→ボタン：02963_botan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{点字|てんじ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ついて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: The elevator buttons have Braille on them.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{券売機|けんばいき}→券売機：09553_kenbaiki⟧や⟦{缶|かん}→缶：01076_kan⟧⟦ビール→ビール：01015_biiru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{点字|てんじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{表示|ひょうじ}→表示：03143_hyouji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Even station ticket machines and beer cans carry Braille labels.

notes:
Japanese Braille writes kana by sound, six dots to a cell; it was devised by {石川倉次|いしかわくらじ} and adopted in 1890. Everyday Braille does not represent kanji.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {点字|てんじ}⟦ブロック→ブロック：05902_burokku⟧: tactile paving (the yellow raised blocks for blind pedestrians)
- {点字|てんじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧: to write in Braille
- {点字|てんじ}⟦{図書館|としょかん}→図書館：00580_toshokan⟧: Braille library
